Bookend

Book club, on your own time, and without the books you just don't want to read.

Veohnti Afokpa · MGT 409 final project · five AI agents on gpt-6-luna

Code (public GitHub repo): https://github.com/veohnti/bookend

The problem

You finished a book. Now what?

"I just finished it."Your partner and friends are reading different books, and the thoughts you have right now are gone by next week.
"I'd join a book club, but…"One book on the list sounds great. The other eleven don't. So you don't join.
"Has anyone read this?"You ask 200 friends. The one who did read it two years ago and forgot the characters' names.

About 3 in 4 U.S. adults read a book last year (Pew Research Center, 2021). Most have no one to talk to the day they finish.

What's new

Matched by when you finished

  • Same book, your window: everyone who finished it in the last week, month, or year, in any edition.
  • No club, no schedule, no assigned books. Everyone already finished, so spoilers are welcome.
  • Booksy when nobody's around: grounded in the catalog, and says when it isn't sure.
  • Safe by default for chatting with strangers.

Compared with Goodreads, StoryGraph buddy reads, Fable and Bookclubs.com clubs, Reddit, and ChatGPT.

Safety

Built for strangers

22/22moderation tests right: harassment, hate, self-harm, contact details, spam, and injection. Spoilers allowed.
12/12 off-topicBooksy only talks books: coding, homework, and essays get a friendly redirect and no AI run.
14/14account tests: hashed passwords, private emails, no posting as someone else, sign-up limits.

Injections in chat or hidden in book descriptions were ignored · instruction leaks blocked · no fake books · every decision in an audit trail.
